summary: 14 days of CGM data (98.7% coverage) show overall TIR 86.0% with 5.1% below range. Overnight hypoglycemia is the dominant safety concern. No carbohydrate entries exist, preventing meal-strategy evaluation. Correction-only boluses reveal the current ISF of 56 mg/dL/U is much too low, causing over-correction lows and inappropriate Dynamic ISF adjustments. A profile ISF increase and a reduction of the excessively high max IOB limit are the primary actions needed before adding meal boluses.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage 98.7%, 3995 valid entries, 5-minute cadence, largest gap 65 minutes. Loop status records and full AAPS profile present. No carbohydrate treatment entries.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero carb entries limit later meal-related inferences.

analysis_steps.findings: TBR 5.1% with severe lows down to 41 mg/dL. Overnight TBR peaks at 18.5% (01:00 local). TIR 86.0%, CV 32.6%. Any change must avoid worsening nocturnal hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Missing meal data prevents attribution of lows.

analysis_steps.findings: Targets are appropriate. Early-night lows suggest excess insulin relative to need. Late-afternoon basal dip (0.5 U/h) may contribute to pre-evening highs, but meal and correction effects cannot be separated. Keep basal rates; validate with fasting tests later.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No fasting windows isolated from meals/corrections; GLP-1 influence not quantified.

analysis_steps.findings: CR and DIA unverifiable without carb entries. Correction-only boluses show insulin effect far exceeding the 56 mg/dL/U ISF (e.g., 0.2 U → -178 mg/dL). Profile ISF is too low; increasing it is the highest priority profile change.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carb data for CR/DIA; Dynamic ISF confounds true ISF need.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM enabled with safe frequency/strength. Low profile ISF combined with UAM/SMB risks over-stacking; the automation is not the root cause of lows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No COB data to test carb-based SMB rules.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF correctly adjusts but worsens situation because base ISF is too low. Max IOB (25 U) is excessive relative to daily insulin (~20 U) and poses a stacking risk once meal boluses are added. Set max IOB to 7 U. Other limits (max basal, absorption model) are acceptable.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal records to validate absorption settings.

analysis_steps.findings: Zero carb entries and no declared meal strategy; prebolus and CR cannot be assessed. Post-breakfast and afternoon rises cannot be attributed to meals.
No e-carb entries or declared parameters. Absorption model defaults cannot be validated.

Profile ISF increase to 100 mg/dL/U is the primary change. Reducing max IOB to 7 U eliminates a latent safety risk. All other profile and automation settings remain unchanged pending meal data. Sequential order: ISF first, then max IOB, then start carbohydrate logging; only after several weeks of logging evaluate basal, CR, and meal strategies.

strengths: Automation (SMB, Dynamic ISF) partially compensates, preventing worse outcomes.
issues: Frequent overnight hypoglycemia (TBR up to 18.5%) driven by a profile ISF that is too low.
Profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U leads to over-correction; Dynamic ISF compounds the error.

recommendations.title: Increase profile ISF
recommendations.description: Correction-only boluses show a much higher real-world ISF than 56 mg/dL/U. Raising ISF to 100 mg/dL/U will reduce over-correction and hypoglycemia risk while allowing Dynamic ISF to function correctly.

recommendations.title: Reduce max IOB to 7 U
recommendations.description: Current max IOB of 25 U is excessive given a total daily insulin of ~20 U. A cap of 7 U prevents severe stacking when meal boluses are eventually introduced, with no impact on current closed-loop delivery.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Increase ISF from 56 mg/dL/U to 100 mg/dL/U using the profile flat ISF segment.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Observed correction boluses (e.g. 0.2 U causing drops > 100 mg/dL) indicate real insulin sensitivity is far higher than the current ISF suggests. An initial ISF of 100 mg/dL/U will align the profile with actual responses, reduce hypoglycemia risk, and allow reliable Dynamic ISF adjustments.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After applying the new ISF, monitor correction-only bolus responses over 3-5 days. A 1-unit correction should produce a glucose drop of approximately 36 mg/dL within 2-3 hours under stable conditions.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Do not introduce meal boluses yet. First correct the profile ISF (to 100 mg/dL/U) and reduce max IOB to 7 U. Then begin logging all carbohydrate intake in Nightscout without changing bolus settings. After 2 weeks of logging, evaluate morning and afternoon glucose patterns to decide a prebolus timing (likely 10-15 minutes) and an initial immediate bolus of 100% (split only if data shows late postprandial lows). Use existing CR values as a starting point. e-carbs are not needed until standard bolusing is established.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The highest risk is hypoglycemia from over-correction due to an inaccurate ISF. Until that is fixed, any meal bolus could cause severe lows. Reliable carbohydrate logs are a prerequisite for CR, prebolus, and e-carb optimisation.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record all meals (grams of carbs) in Nightscout for 14 days after ISF change. Then assess postprandial excursions and correction responses to refine CR and timing.

implementation_steps: 1. Change profile ISF from 56 mg/dL/U to 100 mg/dL/U in the flat ISF segment. Monitor correction-only bolus responses for 3-5 days; a 1-unit correction should produce a drop of ~36 mg/dL.
2. Reduce max IOB from 25 U to 7 U (keep max basal 12 U/h). This safety cap will have no effect on current delivery but protects future scenarios.
3. Begin entering all carbohydrate intake (grams) in Nightscout immediately. Use the existing CR values for now.
4. After 2 weeks of complete meal logging and stable ISF, perform fasting basal tests overnight and late afternoon to decide if basal rates need adjustment (focus on 00:00-05:00 and 16:00-18:00).
5. Once basal is verified, evaluate postprandial excursions to adjust CR and decide prebolus timing. Introduce e-carbs only if extended absorption patterns are evident.
education: ISF (Insulin Sensitivity Factor) defines how much 1 unit of insulin lowers glucose. A value that is too low (e.g., 56 mg/dL/U) tells the system to give more insulin than needed, causing over-correction and hypoglycemia.
Dynamic ISF automatically adjusts the ISF based on recent glucose data, but it starts from the profile ISF. If the profile ISF is wrong, Dynamic ISF will amplify the error.
Max IOB is a safety limit; it should be set just above the highest IOB you normally see. 25 U with a daily total of ~20 U allows severe stacking; a cap of 7 U is much safer.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. All proposed changes must be independently verified, made one at a time, and accompanied by close glucose monitoring.
Discuss any profile or AAPS setting change with your healthcare team before applying it. TuneMyBG does not provide medical advice.
When changing ISF, observe correction boluses carefully; if lows persist, raise ISF further. If corrections are insufficient, gradually lower ISF.
Never change multiple insulin-delivery settings (ISF, basal, CR) at the same time.
